cover.headline: Advanced, measured. Chan validated Zach's Maya read as 'spot on'; the governance/data-sovereignty convergence was the peak. Close was warm but time-boxed with no concrete next step locked.
cover.subline: A genuinely positive, substantive conversation that landed a half-notch below the exceptional Mike round. Three pre-call-flagged gaps resolved live and well: governance/local-first became the strongest mutual-conviction moment (the JD's thinnest bucket from the Mike round), team-leadership got a concrete Grayscale answer, and Zach's unprompted Maya hypotheses were confirmed by the CDO. But two pre-call disciplines were not followed — Zach presented the build-record/hypotheses live (screen-share) rather than handing off the page at close as planned, and led with the framework register rather than the recommended segment-6 situational one. Both recovered by accuracy, not by plan. Chan's real evaluation axis surfaced clearly: institutional harness ('a person can do a lot, but for an enterprise, all those people going off doing cool stuff doesn't advance the cause... how do you harness it?'), not individual technical brilliance. NYC 3-day commute — the pre-call's #1 predicted surprise — again did not come up and remains unresolved two rounds in.

loadBearingQuote.text: What you were able to gather up about the philosophy and the intent of Maya is spot on... the fact that we are in a commercial setting, therefore what we do with it both internally and externally has to be quantifiable impact — revenue, time saved, or quality of work bettered.
loadBearingQuote.attribution: GRANOLA TRANSCRIPT · CHAN SUH (PROPHET, CDO) · JUL 17, 2026
loadBearingQuote.significance: The CDO confirming, unprompted, that Zach's hypotheses about Maya's philosophy and intent — formed from only a press release, the JD, and two prior calls — were accurate. This is the ARCS product thesis proven live in the room: structured see/hear/confirm discovery producing a correct read of a domain Zach had no inside access to. It parallels the Mike round's independent-convergence quote, but is stronger in one way (it's the senior evaluator validating Zach's read, not Zach discovering a shared abstraction) and weaker in another (Chan immediately reframed to the commercial bar — 'quantifiable impact' — which is the altitude he actually evaluates at). Lead future Chan touches from that quantifiable-impact framing, not from build velocity.

statedVsRevealed.stated: Pre-call briefing (precall-chan-suh): open by reading Chan's orientation, do NOT re-run the Mike deep-ARCS/framework recap, default to the segment-6 situational (Prophet/MAIA-specific, business-outcome) register, and hand off chan.arcs.care at the close — 'do NOT walk him through it live (that would repeat the Mike register at page scale).'
statedVsRevealed.revealed: Chan took the open himself ('tell me your journey + what you'd want a year from now'). Zach then ran a prepared, screen-shared hypothesis presentation (see/hear/confirm) plus the build-record/commit walkthrough — the more presentation-forward Mike register, and effectively a live narration of the leave-behind's substance rather than a handoff. It LANDED ('spot on'), so the deviation was recovered by hypothesis accuracy. But the specific discipline the pre-call prescribed was not applied; the recovery came from content quality, not from the plan.
statedVsRevealed.read: Not a failure — but the single most important calibration note. Against an AI-fluent evaluator, the live-narration register cost exactly one beat ('so you had Claude Code generate the Python — that's what it does best'). Accuracy bailed it out this time; do not assume it always will.

statedVsRevealed.axis: Zach's self-narrative vs. demonstrated behavior — sales
statedVsRevealed.stated: Zach: 'What I'm not as in love with is the sales and new-business part of it... figuring out where my circle of competency can end and another person can begin.'
statedVsRevealed.revealed: Zach ran a full, polished consultative sales motion on Chan — discovery, hypotheses, confirm, close — and did it well enough that the CDO called the read 'spot on.' The 'I don't love sales' framing materially understates a demonstrated discovery/positioning capability.
statedVsRevealed.read: A revealed strength, not a contradiction to worry about. But be aware the modesty framing can read as either authentic or as hedging; the transcript shows the capability is real, so own it rather than pre-disclaiming it.

statedVsRevealed.axis: Stated evaluation topic vs. real axis underneath
statedVsRevealed.stated: Chan's surface questions: 'how comfortable you'd be in an employee situation' and 'you didn't mention the actual technical building.'
statedVsRevealed.revealed: Chan's real worry, voiced in the AI-for-institutions riff: 'AI and Claude Code is optimizing for individual achievements. A person can do a lot of things. But for an enterprise that needs to harness a lot of people... all of those people going off doing exploratory cool stuff doesn't necessarily advance the cause. How do you harness it? How do you make it safe?' The employee/technical questions were proxies for one axis: can this solo-founder make AI advance a collective enterprise cause, not just individual velocity.
statedVsRevealed.read: This is the belief shift to internalize. The fit question is institutional harness, not individual brilliance. Zach answered it well in the moment (human-on-the-bike, extending org discipline, uniting disparate teams) but should LEAD from it next time rather than arriving there via the solo-build story.

callWalk.label: RAPPORT OPEN — GYM / KIDS / FUNCTIONAL STRENGTH
callWalk.summary: Warm, unforced open: Zach's gym knee injury, a 5.5-year-old and a 15-month-old, Chan's three sedentary weeks; Zach's post-40 shift to strength/mobility/balance 'so I can keep up with my kids.' Genuine peer rapport, no performance.

callWalk.label: CAREER ARC (3-PART) — CHAN DRIVES THE OPEN
callWalk.summary: Chan takes the wheel ('tell me your journey... and what you'd like to be doing a year from now'), pre-empting Zach's planned orientation question. Zach gives the three-part arc: builder (ad tech / DTC e-commerce / boutique hospitality) → decade of zero-to-one in regulated industries (Grayscale $7B, WTA, rare-disease nonprofits, behavioral-health PE turnaround) → found the Prophet role via his own algorithm. mp3.com/producer origin, an agency.com nod to Chan directly.
callWalk.divergenceFlag: MED — long but responsive to an open prompt; Chan pulled on the 'series of short stints, searching for something' thread, which sets up segment 3.

callWalk.label: EMPLOYEE-vs-ENTREPRENEUR PROBE — THE REAL AXIS (1st surfacing)
callWalk.summary: Chan: 'you've been entrepreneurial a while... short stints... searching for something?' and then directly 'how comfortable you'd be in an employee situation, because you've been ahead of your own firm for a while.' Zach: circle of competency / zones of genius overlap, the isolation of solo founding, wanting a team to bounce ideas off, not loving the sales/new-business part. Honest and well-differentiated.
callWalk.divergenceFlag: LOW — genuinely responsive; this is Chan's true evaluation axis, not the tech.

callWalk.label: TECHNICAL-BUILDING PROBE — MILD DEFLATION SIGNAL
callWalk.summary: Chan: 'you didn't mention the actual technical building.' Zach: music/CS hybrid (Berklee-meets-MIT-Media-Lab program), hacking from a young age, bilingual PM/eng bridge, the ARCS change-control / instant-replay / anti-revisionist-history pitch, and the open-telemetry system he built 'yesterday' from the monorepo commits (Cloud Code + Python + Prisma RLS + Supabase + Vercel). Chan's tell: 'So you had Claude Code generate the Python. That's what it does best.'
callWalk.divergenceFlag: MED — the framework narrative re-surfaces here (the register the pre-call cautioned against), and Chan's flat 'that's what it does best' is the one place an AI-fluent evaluator lightly discounted the build-velocity flex.

callWalk.label: TEAM-LEADERSHIP PROBE — MIKE-ROUND GAP CLOSED
callWalk.summary: Chan: 'experience running teams?' Zach works backward from Grayscale: forward-deployed embedded product lead over four workstreams (front-end UI/UX agency mid-rebrand + design-system tokens/components, legacy CMS tech-debt paydown, headless-CMS + React-Native retool, end-to-end sprint delivery), ~$250k/mo resource value supporting $7B in digital assets; internal+external pods, QA automation, global 24h coverage; ~20 years of it.
callWalk.divergenceFlag: LOW — concrete and specific; directly closes the team-leadership/delivery-cadence gap flagged as undemonstrated in the Mike round.

callWalk.label: PREPARED HYPOTHESIS PRESENTATION + PHILOSOPHICAL CONVERGENCE
callWalk.summary: Zach screen-shares his see/hear/confirm hypotheses on Maya: augmenting (not replacing) intelligence, productizing a dogfooded platform on client demand, cross-offer pattern reuse (campaign tool vs. brand-strategy tool sharing back-end workflow), fire-hose→governance/guardrails, trust-as-a-feature, calibration/belief-change as white space. Chan: 'spot on,' then reframes to the commercial bar (quantifiable impact). The exchange deepens into LLM lock-in / data sovereignty / local-first — Chan's own strongest convictions ('I'd rather it leaked in AWS than inside an LLM company'). Zach matches: NOTOMATION / human-on-the-bike, local-first zero-trust, token-price gouging + fiduciary responsibility (Alex Karp), on-device deterministic compute with a line of demarcation for LLM-touching data.
callWalk.divergenceFlag: LOW — the substantive peak of the call; the governance/sovereignty convergence is real and is Zach's genuine credential. The only MED note is that the live walkthrough was the pre-call plan-deviation.

callWalk.label: CLOSE — MEASURED, TIME-BOXED, SOFT CONTINUATION
callWalk.summary: Zach asks a sharp closing question (what success looks like at 6/12/24 months; how the Foundry/Maya evolves). Chan answers substantively: Foundry = internal platform + agents + workflows for own usage (take-up/usage rate = success); commercial = subscription agents/workflows for clients; the role is product-portfolio management as much as people/resource management; a SaaS tech partner (Lyzr-style) sits underneath Maya; 'triage fast, work well with me as program owner, keep everyone pointed the same way, ship apps, always make things better.' Zach offers more time; Chan declines — hard stop for a call he's hosting — and defers: 'we can pick it up again... let me go work with Cassandra, maybe we can create some more time.'
callWalk.divergenceFlag: MED — read backward, the trajectory was building toward mutual fit, but the landing was a measured, time-boxed deferral with no concrete next step locked. Warm and genuine, but distinctly cooler than the Mike round's interviewer-driven overrun and same-day fast-track.
